added_models.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen

engagement.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen
engagement.note: Merck's rat FFA-reduction screen, run with sibling tricyclic full agonists two years before MK-1903 (itself a tricyclic) was published in it.
engagement.short: Merck rat FFA screen, sibling agonists
engagement.quote: Compound 2g displayed a good therapeutic index regarding free fatty acids (FFA) reduction and vasodilation effects in rats, with very weak cytochrome P450 2C8 (CYP2C8) and cytochrome P450 2C9 (CYP2C9) inhibition, and a good mouse pharmacokinetics (PK) profile.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Compound 2g is a sibling HCAR2 full agonist, not a member; the same screen later carried MK-1903 (Boatman 2012) and SCH 900271 (Palani 2012).
engagement.judgement: Opener. Dated to the earliest public use of Merck's rat FFA/vasodilation screen for this mechanism (sibling 2g); MK-1903's own rat datum was public only in April 2012.

engagement.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen
engagement.note: MK-1903 lowered rat plasma FFA 90 % and single doses above 50 mg lowered healthy-volunteer FFA 90 % within 1-2 h; SCH 900271 likewise.
engagement.short: Acute FFA fell in humans as in rats
engagement.quote: Compound R,R-19a was advanced into a phase 1 clinical trial and produced a robust decrease in plasma free fatty acids.
engagement.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. The rat -90 % and the phase 1 -90 % (doses >50 mg, 1-2 h, lasting 8 h) are read through Tuteja & Duffy 2016 (PMC4773474), a review pointing at Boatman's full text. SCH 900271's rat FFA -70 %/TG -49 % at 1 h sits in Palani 2012's unreadable full text; its human acute FFA fall is Lauring 2012's abstract.
engagement.magnitude_basis: peak plasma FFA suppression: rat 90 % vs phase 1 healthy volunteers 90 % at single doses >50 mg (both numbers via Tuteja & Duffy 2016 from Boatman 2012)
engagement.reason: Rat FFA call held acutely in humans
engagement.judgement: The sponsor paper carries both the rat and the phase 1 FFA data and its title states the human result, so comparison_stated true even though only the abstract is readable. Acute suppression is what the rat measured (1 h post-dose); Lauring 2012 (Aug 2012) adds that chronic FFA suppression was not sustained, the same partial reading the draft gives the knockout-mouse and dog tracks. MK-1903 phase 1 has no registry record.

dose.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen
dose.note: The rat screen set a therapeutic index of FFA reduction over vasodilation, not a human exposure target; nothing to compare before dosing.
dose.short: Rat index, no human exposure yet
dose.quote: Compound 2g displayed a good therapeutic index regarding free fatty acids (FFA) reduction and vasodilation effects in rats, with very weak cytochrome P450 2C8 (CYP2C8) and cytochrome P450 2C9 (CYP2C9) inhibition, and a good mouse pharmacokinetics (PK) profile.

dose.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen
dose.note: Human doses reached the rat's PD target (90 % FFA suppression) yet the phase 2 lipid effect was weak; Merck stopped MK-1903.
dose.short: FFA target reached, lipids failed, stopped
dose.quote: Because R,R-19a produced only a weak effect on serum lipids as compared with niacin, we conclude that the beneficial effects of niacin are most likely the result of an undefined GPR109a independent pathway.
dose.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Preclinical tolerability is stated ('well tolerated, no apparent safety concerns') without a numeric margin, so margin_stated false.
dose.judgement: Reached-failed-abandoned row, as the draft scores the knockout-mouse and dog tracks in the same year. The rat's PD target was met in phase 1 (FFA -90 %) and the phase 2A (NCT00847197, posted 2010-09-22) found no LDL-C change; Boatman's conclusion is the sponsor's own statement that the FFA-to-lipids prediction failed. SCH 900271 (rat FFA -70 %, Palani 2012) followed the same path in the phase 2B (NCT00941603).

efficacy.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen
efficacy.note: Rat FFA suppression stood in for lipid efficacy under the FFA hypothesis; no member agonist had reached dyslipidaemic patients.
efficacy.quote: Compound 2g displayed a good therapeutic index regarding free fatty acids (FFA) reduction and vasodilation effects in rats, with very weak cytochrome P450 2C8 (CYP2C8) and cytochrome P450 2C9 (CYP2C9) inhibition, and a good mouse pharmacokinetics (PK) profile.

efficacy.model: Rat plasma FFA (and TG) suppression after oral agonist, Merck / Schering-Plough screen
efficacy.note: MK-1903 phase 2A: LDL-C co-primary null (+0.2 % vs placebo), HDL-C +4.6 %, a fraction of niacin; SCH 900271 phase 2B likewise.
efficacy.short: Rat FFA did not predict lipid efficacy
efficacy.quote: Because R,R-19a produced only a weak effect on serum lipids as compared with niacin, we conclude that the beneficial effects of niacin are most likely the result of an undefined GPR109a independent pathway.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Patient numbers are the registry rows (NCT00847197 posted 2010-09-22; NCT00941603 posted 2016-04-12) and Lauring 2012's abstract.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: co-primary LDL-C % change vs placebo at week 4: +0.2 % (P=0.93) against the niacin-like -10 to -20 % the FFA hypothesis implied; HDL-C co-primary +4.6 % (P=0.013) vs niacin's ~15-25 %

patient_trials.quote: Percent Change From Baseline in LDL-C (week 4): MK1903 -0.3 (SD 16.3), Placebo -1.5 (SD 12.9); mean difference 0.2 (95% CI -3.9 to 4.3), P=0.926.
Change From Baseline in Direct LDL-C at Week 8: SCH 900271 15 mg -2.0, 10 mg -1.5, 5 mg -4.2, 2.5 mg 0.2, 1 mg 1.2, Placebo 1.5; 15 mg vs placebo -3.5 (P=0.06).

efficacy.reason: Weak lipid effect versus niacin, abandoned
efficacy.judgement: Dated 2012 because MK-1903's own rat datum was public only with Boatman (Apr 2012); a reader pairing the sibling-based rat prediction (Shen 2009) with the 2010 registry posting would date it 2010, still contra. Scored on the LDL-C co-primary as the draft does on its other tracks; HDL-C +4.6 % and TG -10.3 % moved in the predicted direction but below the niacin bar, and the sponsor abandoned both members.

engagement.model: Wild-type mouse dermal blood-flow (vasodilation / flushing) model after oral agonist, Merck
engagement.note: Merck's mouse vasodilation model, used to rank full agonists by flush window against niacin; first published with sibling anthranilides.
engagement.short: Merck mouse flush model, sibling agonists
engagement.quote: Compound 2i exhibited good in vivo antilipolytic efficacy while providing a significantly improved therapeutic index over vasodilation (flushing) with respect to niacin in the mouse model.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Compound 2i is a sibling HCAR2 full agonist, not a member; the readout is cutaneous vasodilation, which Tuteja & Duffy 2016 describe as dermal blood flow for MK-1903.
engagement.judgement: Opener. A pharmacological wild-type mouse dosed with the agonist is a different system from the Gpr109a knockout (niacin, receptor-dependence) the draft tracks, even though both read cutaneous blood flow.

engagement.model: Wild-type mouse dermal blood-flow (vasodilation / flushing) model after oral agonist, Merck
engagement.note: MK-1903 raised mouse dermal blood flow 30 %; dosed patients showed vascular (36 % vs 11 %) and skin (28 % vs 3 %) events.
engagement.short: Mouse vasodilation readout moved in patients
engagement.quote: Vascular disorders: MK1903 42/116, Placebo 8/75; Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders: MK1903 32/116, Placebo 2/75.
engagement.confidence_note: Registry reports system-organ-class rows only, without the term flushing. The mouse +30 % is in Boatman 2012's paywalled full text, read through Tuteja & Duffy 2016. Lauring 2012's phase 1 urinary PGD-M dose-linear rise (the cleaner PD readout) is in an unreadable body.
engagement.magnitude_basis: mouse dermal blood flow +30 % vs patient vascular/skin adverse-event incidence; no common scale
engagement.reason: Cutaneous vasodilation appeared in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Boatman 2012 (mouse, model side public Apr 2012, which sets the year) vs the MK-1903 phase 2A AE rows (posted 2010-09-22). The flush readout is the model's PD readout, so the same registry rows carry engagement and safety; the harm is counted once, in safety.

safety.model: Wild-type mouse dermal blood-flow (vasodilation / flushing) model after oral agonist, Merck
safety.note: Mouse vasodilation model predicts on-target flushing and ranks agonists by their window over niacin; no member in patients yet.
safety.short: Mouse flush window, no patients yet
safety.quote: Compound 2i exhibited good in vivo antilipolytic efficacy while providing a significantly improved therapeutic index over vasodilation (flushing) with respect to niacin in the mouse model.

safety.model: Wild-type mouse dermal blood-flow (vasodilation / flushing) model after oral agonist, Merck
safety.note: Mouse predicted MK-1903 flushes (+30 % dermal blood flow); patients had vascular events 36 % vs 11 %, skin events 28 % vs 3 %.
safety.short: MK-1903 flushed patients as mouse predicted
safety.quote: Vascular disorders: MK1903 42/116, Placebo 8/75; Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders: MK1903 32/116, Placebo 2/75.
safety.confidence_note: Registry rows are system-organ-class counts without the term flushing; Lauring 2012 Tables S2/S3 (MK-1903 AEs) and the Offermanns 2012 Focus sentence that MK-1903 'produced a flushing response similar to that of nicotinic acid' could not be read, so whether the mouse's window over niacin held is unverified.
safety.magnitude_basis: mouse dermal blood flow +30 % vs patient vascular/skin adverse-event incidence; no common scale, and the mouse gives no incidence
safety.judgement: Paired by me: Boatman 2012 mouse (+30 % dermal blood flow, via Tuteja & Duffy 2016) vs NCT00847197 AE rows. Direction held: the model said MK-1903 flushes and patients flushed. If Lauring's Table S2 or the Offermanns Focus shows niacin-like flushing against a mouse claim of a reduced window, this becomes same + partial (window misplaced) on the dog track's pattern; not readable here.

considered_not_added: Identity call, rat vs the Gpr109a knockout mouse and the beagle dog: split. Tracks are systems (species x preparation x readout), not predictions. The knockout is a genetic receptor-dependence model dosed with niacin (product_in_model false); the dog is Schering-Plough's pharmacological screen carrying the flush window; the rat is Merck's own potency screen dosed with the product. They were run by different groups at different times and fail independently (the dog's 'no overt flushing' missed while every FFA call held), so pooling would let one system's miss colour another's; the same acute-FFA prediction is the cell-level question each track answers, as the draft already does for rat-gp-nefa-gsk vs beagle-dog-merck.

Pooling with the existing rat-gp-nefa-gsk track: not done. That track is GSK's two-species (rat + guinea pig) NEFA package first public in 2015 with GSK256073; the Merck/Schering-Plough rat work is 2009-2012 with MK-1903 and SCH 900271, a different sponsor and protocol, and includes a vasodilation readout. Pooling would re-date an existing track to 2009 and the task admits only systems with no track. If the adjudicator reads identity as species + readout, the two rat tracks could be merged with model_first_use_year 2009.

Lauring 2012 SCH900271 phase 1B (10 mg/day vs 2 g/day ER-niacin vs placebo, 4 weeks, n=22/25/24; HDL-C about +10 % vs placebo, no NASTy symptoms, per Tuteja & Duffy 2016): a patient-side in-trial niacin comparator for the existing beagle-dog-merck track (safety 4, efficacy 6), not a model system. No registry record (CT.gov intr search finds only NCT00941603); the body and Tables S5-S7 are not served, so it cannot be quoted. Left to the adjudicator.

Lauring 2012 Fig. S1 (SCH900271 preclinical pharmacology summary) and Tables S2-S3 (MK-1903 phase 2A adverse events): unreadable; they bear on existing tracks (dog comparison_stated; dating of the knockout mouse flush 'same') and on the mouse flush track's partial/window question, not on a new system.

Merck rat vasodilation readout (Shen 2009 compound 2g; Shen 2010 MK-6892 'rats and dogs'): same rat system, but the flush readout was published only for non-member siblings; no member-drug rat flush datum is public, so the rat track carries no safety cell.
MK-6892 (Shen 2010, 10.1021/jm100022r), rat and dog FFA vs vasodilation window: non-member preclinical candidate with no patient data.
Beagle dog data for MK-1903, if in Boatman 2012's paywalled full text: would be entries on the existing beagle-dog-merck track, not a new system.
Lauring 2012 humanized LDLR-/- mouse with or without GPR109A dosed with MK-1903: already tracked (mouse-ldlr-humanized-lauring, retro).

GSK256073 type 2 diabetes trials (NCT01147861 phase 1, NCT01376323 12-week phase 2; Dobbins 2013/2015) and the healthy-volunteer food-effect study NCT00808093: cross-indication patient-side data, not a model system; the GSK rat/guinea-pig and guinea-pig ear tracks already exist.
Human genetic model (HCAR2 loss-of-function or flush-variant carriers): no cohort compared with a member drug found.
In-silico / PBPK / PK-PD or occupancy models for any member: none found in Europe PMC.

Patient-derived or ex-vivo adipocyte lipolysis: the member papers' in-vitro work is recombinant hu-GPR109a cell assays (Palani EC50 2 nM; Boatman), not patient-derived, and no patient comparison was found.
Golden Syrian hamster diet-induced hyperlipidaemia (ARI-3037MO, Connolly 2011 abstract) and the monkey in Tuteja Table 1 (a niacin prodrug): non-members; ARI-3037's HCAR2 agonism is undisclosed.
Offermanns 2012 Focus (10.1126/scitranslmed.3004445): a commentary, used as a pointer only; its MK-1903 flushing sentence could not be verified against the page.
